regions.text: For I have sworn before you and
regions.explanation: From 8.46s to 11.10s (“For I have sworn before you and”), articulation rate slowed to 3.04 syll/s against 4.76 syll/s in the reference (-36%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.

regions.text: solemn oath our forebears prescribed nearly a century and three quarters ago.
regions.explanation: From 12.60s to 16.17s (“solemn oath our forebears prescribed nearly a century and …”), 3 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 370 ms to 0 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.
